name: Momo the Missouri Monster
description: Momo (the Missouri Monster) is a Bigfoot-type cryptid reportedly seen near Louisiana, Missouri in the early 1970s, most famously during a brief 'monster flap' in July 1972.
full_description: Momo, an abbreviation of Missouri Monster, is a regional Bigfoot-type cryptid associated with the area around Louisiana, Missouri, in northeastern Missouri (Pike County) along the Mississippi River. Witnesses described a large, hair-covered, bipedal creature roughly seven feet tall, with a 'pumpkin-shaped' head, glowing orange eyes, and a strong putrid smell. The most widely publicised sightings occurred in July 1972, including a 11 July 1972 incident in which two young brothers playing in their backyard and their older sister, who saw the creature from the kitchen window, reported a hairy creature carrying a dead dog. Local fire chief and city council member Richard Allan Murray was among other witnesses. A roughly 20-person posse searched the area but found no specimen. The active sighting period was brief and Momo became a fixture of regional folklore and 1970s American 'monster flap' culture, including a Six Flags theme-park ride (1973-1994) and a 2019 docudrama film.
origin: Highly localised to the area around Louisiana, Missouri, in Pike County, Missouri, along the Mississippi River.

etymology.origin: American journalistic shorthand: 'Mo.' for Missouri + 'Mo.' for Monster, contracted to 'Momo'.
etymology.first_use: 1972, in U.S. press coverage of the Louisiana, Missouri sightings.
